primary_goal: human preference for what to retain and when to use it; answer accuracy is secondary
primary_human_endpoint: blinded human preference over complete dialogue memory use behavior; retention choice is an intermediate observation

arms.read_only: full dialogue state; score on disposable forks
arms.replacement: rebuild from latest three completed exchanges plus current user turn and carried valid cards
arms.feedback: continue appraisal state; write selected cards at a clean turn boundary

candidate_generation_scope: fixture-supplied cards, quotes, item mapping, and versions; raw-dialogue extraction/attribution/deduplication/version detection not evaluated

short_pilot.tie_break: descending unrounded priority then lexicographic memory_id; may bias equal-score selection
short_pilot.runtime_work_scope: includes appraisal prompts and unscored control replay; excludes latency and peak memory

long_window_pair.tie_break: descending unrounded priority then lexicographic memory_id
long_window_pair.runtime_work_scope: includes appraisal prompts and unscored control replay; excludes latency and peak memory

limits: Synthetic dialogue only; curator labels are not human preference ratings.
Replay scores fixture-supplied candidate cards only; extraction, attribution, deduplication, versioning, and evidence generation are not evaluated.
Replay generates no assistant replies and performs no archive retrieval.
State strategies differ in history window, card placement, and number of forwarded tokens; outcomes cannot be attributed to a tensor operation alone.
RWKV label probabilities and confidence are not calibrated probabilities of human agreement.
Equal unrounded priority scores are broken by lexicographic memory ID; this can bias selection and is reported explicitly.
Explicit card-write tokens are only one component of inference cost; wall-clock latency and peak memory were not measured.

The expiry fixture removes old versions by supplied ID. The old deadline was selected only by the read-only arm before correction; neither persistent arm wrote it, so retirement of a previously carried card was not tested.
A working-memory card is not a full transcript archive; low retention must not be described as transcript deletion.
